text:
maria: Quick follow-up after the RFC — I ran a smoke test and hit a couple handshake edge cases when older clients call the new /generate path. Logging a thread so we can decide a minimal shim strategy.

jon: Which edge cases? can you paste a failing request?

maria: Old mobile SDKs send no Accept-Version or X-Api-Version and rely on content-type + path. Our new router assumes Accept-Version: 3 and returns 426 in some flows. Example captured: 
```http
POST /v3/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Accept: */*
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx

{"prompt":"hi"}
```

kevin: So the client thinks it's v3 because of the path, but our middleware checks Accept-Version header first and rejects missing header. That seems like a change of semantics from previous behavior: previously path dominated.

abby: Right. Current deploy changed precedence: header > path > default. That's what broke a few internal SDKs.

maria: One option: quick shim in api-gateway that treats missing Accept-Version as path-derived for any /v[0-9]+/* requests. Minimal, localized.

jon: I like the shim. Low risk, fast rollback. We should also emit a deprecation warning header so clients get telemetry: 
"X-Compat-Warning: missing Accept-Version, deriving from path; please upgrade"

kevin: Agree. Also add a metric counter compat.missing_version_path_derived. We'll be able to track clients that depend on old semantics.

sanjay: For non-versioned paths (e.g., /generate) we still want header-required behavior, right?

maria: Yes. Plan: 1) api-gateway shim: if Accept-Version missing && path matches ^/v(\d+)/, derive version from path and add X-Compat-Warning header + metric. 2) short rollout to 10% traffic, monitor compat.missing_version_path_derived and error rate. 3) after 4 weeks, surface top caller ids for outreach.

abby: What about custom hostnames for Dedicated customers? They sometimes proxy without path versions. We should ensure the shim only runs in hosted gateway, not in dedicated/reverse-proxy.

jon: Good catch. Add gating: only apply shim when request.host in (api.redwood.ai, api-eu.redwood.ai) and not when X-Customer-Hostname present.

kevin: Implementation sketch for gateway (pseudo): 
```js
if (!req.headers['accept-version'] && req.path.match(/^\/v(\d+)\//)) {
  req.headers['accept-version'] = 'v' + RegExp.$1;
  res.setHeader('X-Compat-Warning','missing Accept-Version, deriving from path');
  metrics.increment('compat.missing_version_path_derived');
}
next();
```

maria: Also need to update the docs and SDKs: mobile SDK >= 2.1 will add Accept-Version automatically. We'll schedule a blog + migration guide.

sanjay: Timeline?

maria: Draft shim PR today, gated rollout tomorrow, 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h if no regressions. Outreach list after 2 weeks.

abby: Can we add a temporary compatibility test in ci that simulates old clients to avoid regressions?

jon: Yes — add a test job that sends requests without Accept-Version to v3 path and expects 200 and X-Compat-Warning header. Fail the job if 426/4xx occur.

deploy-bot: deploy-plan created: shard=api-gateway, patch=compat/path-derive, rollout=[10,50,100], owner=maria

kevin: One more tradeoff: deriving from path preserves old semantics but makes headers less authoritative. We should treat this as temporary (90 days) and schedule strict enforcement after migration window.

maria: Agreed. I'll add an expiry date in the warning header: X-Compat-Expires: 2026-07-15. That gives time for customers to upgrade.

jon: I'll review the PR this afternoon. Thanks for surfacing — good low-risk mitigation. :thumbsup:
